research.name: Zero-DCE
research.headline: Low-light enhancement, brought to a DSLR demo.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Low-light enhancement needs to preserve useful detail without amplifying noise or introducing unwanted color shifts.

story.title: Our contribution
story.text: With Farhan Tandia and Martin Dominikus, I worked on extending the original Zero-DCE research with DSLR integration, color correction, denoising, dataset augmentation, and retraining.

story.title: The approach
story.text: The public implementation combines PyTorch enhancement, color balancing, and OpenCV denoising. Node-RED and gPhoto2 connect the DSLR demonstration.

story.title: The result
story.text: Best Demo Award, Applied Computer Vision 2020. The images below are the original and the team’s enhanced result from the public repository; they are a qualitative example, not a new benchmark.

research.summary: Real-time enhancement, color correction, and denoising.

research.name: 2D-to-3D Human Pose
research.headline: The research behind my computer vision career.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Human behavior recognition should account for changes in camera viewpoint, rather than treating each angle as an entirely separate problem.

story.title: My contribution
story.text: As part of my master’s thesis, I extended existing pose-estimation baselines to use AlphaPose inputs, convert COCO joints to Human3.6M, estimate 3D skeletons, and transform skeleton references. Rashid Ali is credited as another contributor.

story.title: The approach
story.text: A PyTorch 2D-to-3D pipeline, Optuna hyperparameter tuning, skeleton-reference transformation, and notebooks for pose visualization. This builds on AlphaPose and the published 3D Pose Baseline implementations.

story.title: The context
story.text: Academic research on human behavior recognition inside elevators with variable camera angles. This public repository is a research artifact, not a current production system.

story.title: From research to engineering
story.text: This thesis work taught me to connect model inputs, coordinate conventions, evaluation, and visualization. Those concerns continue in my professional computer vision work, alongside application and product engineering.

research.summary: Master’s thesis: pose lifting and viewpoint transformation.

research.name: Traffic Jam Prediction
research.headline: Comparing models for West Java traffic reports.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Predict which sectors will receive high traffic-jam reports at particular dates and hours using the competition’s West Java traffic data.

story.title: Our contribution
story.text: With Farhan Tandia, I explored multiple tabular learning approaches and ensemble methods for the Lulus2021 team.

story.title: The approach
story.text: The notebook includes CatBoost, LightGBM, NODE, a PyTorch MLP, FastAI, feature experiments, and ensemble workflows. The README also lists TabNet among the approaches explored.

story.title: The result
story.text: Official private leaderboard: 12th of 96 teams, top 13%. The repository reports a later submission at 5th of 96; that later result is separate from the official competition placement.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Predict employee performance for the following year using historical KPI data in a people-analytics competition.

story.title: Our contribution
story.text: I participated with team PelajarHsinchu. The public repository contains people-analytics preprocessing, boosting experiments, and submission notebooks.

story.title: The approach
story.text: The reviewed CatBoost notebook encodes categorical features, prepares numeric data, uses a held-out validation split, and trains a CatBoost classifier with AUC evaluation.

story.title: The result
story.text: 83rd of 505 teams, top 16%, as reported in the repository. This was a competition exercise; it is not presented as a deployed HR decision system.

research.name: Shopee Product Matching
research.headline: Learning visual similarity between product listings.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Recognize whether two product listings describe the same item, supporting better matching across a marketplace.

story.title: Our contribution
story.text: A collaborative NDSC project with Farhan Tandia, Mahdin Rohmatillah, and Martin Dominikus. I contributed to the team’s product-matching experiments.

story.title: The approach
story.text: The README documents Siamese networks, contrastive loss, EfficientNetB3, augmentation, and optimizer experiments. The checked-in competition notebook uses a shared EfficientNetB6 with pairwise features and binary cross-entropy: these are different experiments.

story.title: The result
story.text: 6th of 139 teams, top 5%, in NDSC Indonesia 2020. The achievement belongs to the team; no single notebook is claimed to explain the entire result.

research.name: Traveling Salesman Problem
research.headline: Searching for shorter routes with evolution.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Visit every city and return to the start while minimizing the total route distance.

story.title: My contribution
story.text: I implemented and explored a genetic algorithm for an Evolutionary Computation course project, with configurable populations, generations, and route visualizations.

story.title: The approach
story.text: Candidate routes compete through binary tournament selection. Crossover and mutation repair repeated cities; fitness evaluation and truncation selection form subsequent populations.

story.title: The context
story.text: An academic optimization experiment. Genetic algorithms search for useful solutions, but this project does not establish a guaranteed global optimum or a production routing service.

research.summary: Genetic algorithms, selection, crossover, and mutation.
